claims.statement: Gov. Spanberger and Virginia Democrats propose, for the 2027 General Assembly, requiring local approval for data centers using more than 25 megawatts, banning nondisclosure agreements with local officials, and tightening oversight of cooling water.

sources.quote: The lawmakers presented several data center proposals, including requirements for local approval of facilities using more than 25 megawatts, a ban on nondisclosure agreements with local officials and stronger oversight of cooling water use.

claims.statement: Dominion's counsel argued at the SCC's merger hearing that the merger case is not the place to decide who pays their fair share, including data centers.

sources.quote: This case, in our view, is simply not the one to litigate that cost of service, and nor is it the case to litigate who’s paying their fair share, and ensuring everybody pays their fair share, including the data centers

claims.statement: The average monthly Dominion residential bill rose from $90.59 on July 1, 2007 to $180.79 on July 1, 2026, an increase of 99.57%.

sources.quote: In a report to the Energy Commission of Virginia, the SCC reported that the average monthly Dominion residential bill “was $90.59 as of July 1, 2007. The bill has increased by $90.20, or 99.57%, to $180.79 per month as of July 1, 2026.”

claims.statement: Residential customers still subsidize too much of the cost of building Virginia's grid for demand driven largely by data centers.

sources.origin: Reps. Beyer, McClellan, Subramanyam, Vindman and Walkinshaw (letter to the SCC)
sources.quote: But the congressional delegation said that too much of the cost to build out the grid in Virginia to support the skyrocketing energy demands, largely driven by data centers, is still subsidized by residential customers.

claims.statement: A coalition of Virginia environmental groups calls for a statewide pause on new data center permits and grid connections until stricter water, energy and siting rules are enacted.

sources.quote: A united front of environmental groups representing all corners of the commonwealth on Wednesday in Hanover urged the state government to implement a statewide pause on all new data center permit approvals and connections to the grid until stricter regulations for water use, energy infrastructure, and siting are enacted.

claims.statement: Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors paused consideration of data center and substation applications for up to 12 months, backdated to September 15, 2026, by a 7-1 vote with one abstention.

sources.quote: The adopted resolution, which passed 7-1 with one abstention, sees the board pause consideration of applications for data centers and substations for a period not to exceed 12 months, effective backdated from September 15, 2026.

claims.statement: Suffolk won't let data center projects move forward until it has rules and restrictions in place.

sources.quote: Suffolk will not allow data center projects to move forward until it has rules and restrictions in place.

claims.statement: A federal indictment unsealed October 22, 2026 alleges that Sen. Louise Lucas led a criminal marijuana distribution enterprise.
claims.unrelated: Mithlond's research tracks Sen. Lucas (research/TASKS.md, track E1). These charges concern a marijuana business; no source connects them to data centers. An indictment is a charge, not a finding of guilt.

sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
sources.origin: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
sources.quote: According to the indictment, Virginia state senator Lillie Louise Lucas, 82, of Portsmouth, Virginia, led a criminal enterprise (the Lucas Enterprise) comprised of a close-knit group of associates and family members, including her two daughters and her grandson.

sources.origin: Sen. Louise Lucas (plea, reported by WTVR CBS 6)
sources.quote: State Sen. Louise Lucas was back in federal court in Newport News Monday, entering a "not guilty" plea against federal charges including racketeering, money laundering and illegally selling marijuana.

claims.statement: Roanoke City Council asked the General Assembly, in its 2027 legislative agenda, for a data center moratorium until public health and consumer protection standards are adopted.

sources.quote: The council’s request, approved as a part of the city’s 2027 legislative agenda this week, asks for the moratorium “until public health and consumer protection standards are adopted to address impacts on energy and water use, drinking water, air and water quality, utility rates, agriculture, parks, historic sites, forests and infrastructure.”

claims.statement: Norfolk is considering zoning rules under which data centers under 30,000 square feet or below 25 MW would be allowed by default, while larger ones would need a conditional use permit with a public hearing (reported by WHRO, from the Planning Director's briefing).

sources.origin: City of Norfolk (Planning Commission recommendation and Planning Director's briefing to City Council)
sources.quote: Data centers under 30,000 square feet or consuming less than 25 megawatts of power would be permitted by default in office, business commerce, industrial and institutional areas. Larger data centers would require a conditional use permit in general industrial, deep waterfront industrial and certain business commerce park districts.

claims.statement: PJM Interconnection has filed a plan with FERC to speed the connection of power plants and data centers, with data centers expected to pay the cost (reported by DatacenterDynamics).

sources.quote: The US’ largest Regional Transmission Operator (RTO), PJM Interconnection, has filed a plan with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to expedite the connection of power plants and data centers, with the latter expected to foot the bill.

claims.statement: The US Senate has passed a bipartisan bill that would require AI data centers to pay a larger share of the cost of the energy infrastructure they need; it now goes to the House (reported by DatacenterDynamics).

sources.quote: The US Senate has passed a bipartisan bill that would require AI data centers to pay a larger share of the cost of building the energy infrastructure they need.

claims.statement: The Data Center Coalition testified to the Loudoun County Board of Supervisors that sweeping moratorium policies do not solve complex infrastructure challenges (reported by Virginia Mercury).

sources.origin: Data Center Coalition (testimony to the Loudoun County Board of Supervisors)
sources.quote: While we recognize that growth can raise important questions that are worthy of public discussion, sweeping policies to impose a moratorium do not solve complex infrastructure challenges

claims.statement: Cardinal News reports that a Botetourt County circuit judge ordered construction on Google's data center project to stop after ruling that the county's board of supervisors violated Virginia's Freedom of Information Act in approving a key agreement.

sources.quote: Construction at the Google data center project in Botetourt County must stop, a circuit judge ordered Monday, after ruling that the county’s board of supervisors violated Virginia’s Freedom of Information Act when it approved a key agreement with the tech giant.
